content.value_statement: Vue Router mistakes can cause stale data, redirect loops, and unreliable navigation. This skill provides focused Vue Router 4 patterns for implementation and review.
actual_capabilities: Explains when route parameter changes bypass per-route guards and lifecycle hooks.
Shows return-based patterns for synchronous and asynchronous navigation guards.
Identifies causes and fixes for infinite redirect loops.
Demonstrates cleanup for hashchange event listeners.
Provides a production Vue Router setup with nested, lazy, and catch-all routes.
Compares component, route-level, and global guard behavior.
limitations: Covers Vue Router 4 and does not target Vue Router 3 behavior.
Provides reference patterns but does not execute or test application code.
Does not replace application-specific authorization or threat modeling.
Examples require adaptation to each project's state and data layers.

use_cases.title: Review Navigation Guards
use_cases.description: Find missing returns, unhandled promises, deprecated callbacks, and redirect loops in Vue Router guards.

use_cases.title: Fix Stale Route Data
use_cases.description: Choose watchers or update guards when reused route components display data for an earlier parameter.

use_cases.title: Plan Production Routing
use_cases.description: Create a maintainable router structure with lazy loading, nested routes, metadata, and fallback handling.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Router Pattern

prompt_templates.scenario: Learning the cause of a routing issue

prompt_templates.prompt: Review this navigation guard for missing returns, deprecated next usage, asynchronous errors, and redirect loops: [paste guard].

prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Vue Router configuration for guard order, authorization flow, redirects, lazy loading, nested routes, cleanup, and error handling: [paste files].

output_examples.input: Why does beforeEnter not run when only the user ID changes?
output_examples.output: The route record remains active, so beforeEnter does not run. Watch the ID or use an in-component route update guard.
Exclude the login route from the authentication redirect and return one final result from each guard path.

output: Register the hashchange listener when the component mounts.
Remove the same listener when the component unmounts.
Use Vue Router when the application needs guards, nested routes, or history support.

best_practices: Return navigation outcomes from guards and await every asynchronous authorization decision.
React directly to route parameter changes when Vue reuses a component instance.
Keep redirects centralized and exclude their destination routes from repeated guard checks.
anti_patterns: Do not rely only on mounted hooks for data tied to changing route parameters.
Do not call next multiple times or mix next callbacks with return-based guard outcomes.
Do not create hashchange listeners without removing them during component cleanup.

faq.question: Which Vue Router version does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on Vue Router 4 for Vue 3 applications.

faq.question: Can it fix redirect loops?
faq.answer: It explains common loop causes and recommends destination exclusions, route metadata, and centralized redirect logic.

faq.question: Does beforeEnter run when route parameters change?
faq.answer: Usually no, when navigation stays on the same route record. Use a watcher, component update guard, or global guard.

faq.question: Does it support asynchronous guards?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers awaited checks, loading states, timeouts, multiple checks, and error handling.

faq.question: Can it test my router automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and examples but does not run tests or inspect a live application.

faq.question: Does it cover simple hash routing?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains listener cleanup and when a production application should adopt Vue Router.
